title: Up to one error
note: One error allowed, so "color" matches. Raise the budget to 2 and "collar" matches too.
subject: the color of the collar

title: A budget per kind of error
note: Each kind of error has its own budget. Every match reports what it spent.
subject: xfoobat

title: Weighted cost
note: A cost equation prices each kind of error. Kinds it never names are free, and the total has to stay under the limit.
subject: 3oifaowefbaoraofuiebofasebfaobfaorfeoaro

title: Edits limited to letters
note: The set after the colon says which characters an edit may touch. Lowercase letters only here, so "color" matches within the budget. "col our" and "col0ur" are missed, because reaching them would spend an error on a space or a digit.
subject: colour, color, col our and col0ur

title: The first match the budget allows
note: An unbounded budget takes the leftmost thing that fits, six substitutions deep. The next two samples do better on this subject.
subject: xirefoabralfobarxie

title: BestMatch: the closest fit
note: BestMatch searches the whole subject for the cheapest match. Same pattern, same subject, one deletion against six substitutions.
subject: xirefoabralfobarxie

title: EnhanceMatch: tighten what was found
note: EnhanceMatch keeps the first match's position and improves the fit there. The span shrinks from six characters to three.
subject: xirefoabralfobarxie

title: Fuzzy matching against a word list
note: A named list supplies literal alternatives beside the pattern. With a budget on top, one pattern covers every word in the list.
subject: aple bananna cherry

title: Leftmost-first
note: By default an alternation takes the first branch that matches at the leftmost position, however short. Perl and .NET do the same.
subject: abcd

title: POSIX: leftmost-longest
note: Under POSIX rules the same pattern takes the longest match at that position, as grep and awk do.
subject: abcd

title: Partial: so far, so good
note: The subject ran out before the pattern did, which is how a search box tells a half-typed entry from a wrong one. Finish the date and the match stops being partial.

title: Search from the right
note: The search starts at the end of the subject, so the first match found is the last one in the text. Only the direction changes.
subject: one two three

title: Replace with a template
note: Templates use upstream's syntax: \1 and \g<name>. A dollar sign is ordinary text here.
subject: 2026-09 and 1999-12

title: Replace a misspelling
note: Fuzzy matching and replacement compose: match within a budget, write the right spelling back.
subject: the color of the collar

title: A pattern that runs out of time
note: This pattern has to try every way of splitting 36 a's before it can answer. The engine gives up after two seconds, and the page stays responsive while it works, because the engine runs in a Web Worker.
subject: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaab

title: Named groups and every capture
note: A repeated group keeps every capture it made. The group table lists them all.
subject: alpha, beta, gamma

title: Set operations
note: One character set subtracted from another: word characters minus digits.
subject: abc123def456

title: Unicode properties
note: A script property matches by what a character is, wherever it sits in an alphabet.
subject: alpha then αβγ then beta

title: Case-insensitive, with a flag
note: Flags are typed by name, so a typo is an error. Take IgnoreCase away and see.
subject: Fuzzy FUZZY fuzzy
